Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).
- Having an MRP is very important for contributors to be able to reproduce the bug in the same way that you are experiencing it. When testing a potential fix for the issue, contributors will use the MRP to validate that the fix is working as intended.
- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available.

Looking in the engine itself  for what happens, (if i understood correctly) (note that i'm new to godot and recently started understanding the engine with the purpose of contributing) it seemes that  a CharacterBody3D is not considered as fully simulated body but a static/kinematic body an thereforeit doesn't  have a PhysicsDirectBodyState  and its physics arent calculated on the server so its gravity is always the default. In other words the total  gravity calculation is done on the physics server and only on the  simulated bodies,  that is why your example works on a rigidBody but not on a characterbody.

Now is this the behavior that was intended? I don't know. But guessing  with the Godot documentation we have this phrase on the CharacterBody3D page " They are not affected by physics " so i would say yes it is intentional. The total gravity is not calculated with the purpose of you  being the one that calculates by scripting "A 3D physics body specialized for characters moved by script.".  

Note again, i'm new to trying to contribute to Godot so my assement could be wrong so i sugest wer wait for somebody that has more knowledge of the engine.

Thanks for looking into the issue.

My point is not that CharacterBody3D should be affected by gravity in default. Instead it is that the func get_gravity() should follow what document says or let's change the document to say some physics bodies, like CharacterBody3D, don't have a combined result from project and area.

As of the CharacterBody3D, it is really by design not affected by gravity in default as you have to manually apply the gravity (which can be derived from get_gravity()) to the velocity and call move_and_slide(). But the get_gravity() returns only the project settings, not a combined result of project settings and area settings, which is the problem my project is facing when I try to apply it to the velocity of player.

Ok so i got an update and a better response to your issue.
First i was wrong in thinking that CharacterBody3D  doesn't have a PhysicsDirectBodyState , it does have one. 
With the help of a more experience contributor  we find out that  the "problem" (problem in quotes because i'm asking in the rocket chat if the behavior is intended) is not that the CharacterBody3D   physics arent computed , the "problem" is that the total gravity is  only computed  when you call move_and_slide() or move_and_collide() so as we can see in the video, once we apply a move_and_slide we get the intended gravity. 

So now the question is, is this a bug or intended? And i agree if it intended then we should modify the documentation to better explain the functionality of get_Gravity() and avoid this confusion and add a remark on the fact that not all the bodies compute gravity the same way.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfe425fe-4d4d-42a5-af8a-70f10fb1a200

You do indeed need to move a kinematic body for its gravity to be updated. This applies when using Jolt Physics as well, although the Jolt implementation seems to at least get an up-to-date initial value, unlike Godot Physics.

I don't believe this was intended, and it was [something I brought up](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/84640#issuecomment-1927117203) in the PR that introduced the `PhysicsBody3D.get_gravity` method, but unfortunately only after it got merged, and then nobody (including myself) ever did anything about it.

The fundamental problem is that we only ever update the gravity for kinematic bodies when they're awake/active (i.e. not `sleeping`), and that's only the case for a single physics frame after moving it.

The only real solutions I can see are:

1. Have kinematic bodies be considered to be awake/active all the time, thus continously updating gravity.
    - This would come at a non-trivial performance cost that I don't think is justified here.
2. Change `PhysicsDirectBodyState3D::get_total_gravity` to calculate gravity as-needed rather than using a cached value, maybe for kinematic bodies only.
    - This would mean doubling down on an already "broken" implementation, since I don't think nodes should be relying on `PhysicsDirectBodyState3D` to begin with, but we've already done so in other places anyway, so might not be a strong argument against it.
3. As mentioned in the comment I linked, set up a state synchronization callback in the `CharacterBody3D` node, much like what you find in `RigidBody3D`, `AnimatableBody3D` and `PhysicalBone3D`, and then change the physics servers to invoke the synchronization callback for all bodies (both dynamic and kinematic) when their area overlaps change.
    - This to me seems like the most proper solution, but again comes at some kind of performance cost, since we're doing extra work, albeit much less than the first solution.
    - The fact that it would get invoked on area overlap changes is arguably weird/arbitrary, but seems like a lesser evil.
    - This also technically changes the behavior of `_integrate_forces` for `RigidBody3D`, as it will now also be invoked when area overlaps change while it's `sleeping`, but I don't think that's too big of a deal. We already call it on the first `sleeping` frame, so the body sleeping needs to be considered anyway.

I guess we should document this behavior if we don't come up with a good solution before 4.6 is released, and we should ideally have documented it when it was first introduced, but we'd be documenting buggy behavior.

Thanks for the efforts!

Is it possible to change func to get_gravity(forced:= false) to return a refreshed result when forced is true?

Otherwise, I do hate performance cost (much like most developers :D) regardless small or big as long as it is unnecessary. So I vote for the document change to let developer have better understanding on the func behavior.

> Is it possible to change func to get_gravity(forced:= false) to return a refreshed result when forced is true?

Probably, but that'd essentially be solution 2, i.e. doubling down on the usage of `PhysicsDirectBodyState*D`, which I would personally prefer we did not do.

> Otherwise, I do hate performance cost (much like most developers :D) regardless small or big as long as it is unnecessary.

Yeah, I must admit I'd be hesitant to push solution 3, no matter how "proper" I find it to be. The state synchronization is already a drag on performance for `RigidBody*D`, and introducing it for kinematic bodies will be no different. I guess the important question would be how many projects out there are relying on hundreds/thousands of `CharacterBody*D` (or `RigidBody*D` using `FREEZE_MODE_KINEMATIC`).

With that said, there would still be _some_ kind of escape hatch for people who don't want to pay that cost, as you could technically create your own kinematic node using the physics server API and simply not hook up a state synchronization callback.
